title: Patience
definition: Patience is Spirit-formed endurance, restraint, and trust while waiting on God and bearing with others in love.
summary: Believers learn patience because God is faithful and graciously patient with them.
christFocus: Jesus Christ patiently endures with His people and teaches them to wait, forgive, and persevere.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Patience describes a Spirit-formed pattern of life for those who belong to Jesus Christ. Christian living is not an attempt to earn salvation but the grateful response of people who have been saved by grace and called to walk with the Lord.

Scripture presents this truth so believers can grow in holiness, endurance, love, wisdom, worship, and mission. It touches the heart, the mind, the tongue, relationships, daily habits, and faithful obedience in ordinary life.

The emphasis of this doctrine is believers learn patience because god is faithful and graciously patient with them.. It points disciples away from self-reliance and toward abiding dependence on Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because discipleship can become shallow when it is reduced to information, emotion, or outward activity alone. Patience teaches believers how grace becomes visible in daily conduct, perseverance, relationships, and obedience to Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask the Lord to form this truth in you through Scripture, prayer, repentance, and faithful practice. Let patience shape how you think, speak, serve, endure, forgive, and represent Christ in the places God has assigned to you.
